notes.note:
I wrote the near pose set for the swordsman in `work/near_poses/cand_1/`: the script, its JSON output and a render. I checked the render by eye. A script check confirmed:
- all joints are in bounds;
- idle 0 and strike 0 are REST exactly;
- death 0 is the same as flinch 0;
- strike 7 is within 2 px of REST and flinch 3 within 1 px.

Nothing outside the folder was touched, and no image calls were made.

**Line of action, strike:**
- 0: rest.
- 1: leans back to the upper-left.
- 2: coiled back to the upper-left, crouched.
- 3: torso whips forward; the front (screen-right) foot steps to the lower-right, to (106,124).
- 4: low and leaning in toward the lower-right.
- 5: same as 4.
- 6: rises.
- 7: settles.

Head, torso and legs come from the mirrored far set, with left and right swapped and moved about 5 px right to line up with the real sprite.

**The swing, near (screen-left) hand:**
- **Frame 1:** the sword lifts beside the head, hand at (63,49), tip up and back at (48,16).
- **Frame 2 (wind-up):** hand high behind the near shoulder at the head's top-left (65,47). The blade is cocked behind the shoulders, tip at (35,65), and drawn behind the body.
- **Frame 3:** the near shoulder twists forward and the arm comes across under the chin. The blade is level, pointing right, tip at (134,73).
- **Frame 4 (contact):** the arm reaches across the front of the body, hand at (101,88). The blade points down-right at about 27°, tip at (132,104), clearly out at the lower-right.
- **Frame 5:** tip nearly on the ground at (121,121).
- **Frame 6:** the blade comes back up to upright.

The shield (far arm) is tucked in during the wind-up and pulled back behind the torso from frame 3.

**Death fall:** in frame 3 he kneels with the sword tip resting on the ground in front of him. In frame 4 he tips back toward the upper-left, the sword drops at the lower-right, the shield arm flies up and the near arm reaches back. From frame 5 he lies on his back along the ground axis, head (51,99) to pelvis (84,115) at about 26°. The sword lies past his feet, the shield lies flat on the far side under his far hand, and he bounces 2 px in frame 6.

**Compromises:**
- In frame 3 the near arm can't reach over the large head, so it crosses under the chin rather than "over the head".
- The shield in frames 4 and 5 still peeks out at the upper-right of the body.
- The flinch and dropped-sword blades are foreshortened (24–31 px against 36), as in the far set.

The near pose set for the lower-right swordsman is finished and renders cleanly. The script checks every frame for bounds, bone lengths, how far the warped frames stray from REST, the REST frames, and death frame 0 matching flinch frame 0, and nothing is flagged.

**Swing choice.** He cuts diagonally down from over his near (right) shoulder. An overhead chop won't work here: the arms are about 17 px long and the head is 26 px across, so the hand can't get above the head. So the near arm swings across the front of the chest and the blade carries the big motion. That arm is the one closest to the viewer, so the arm and blade are drawn over the body and never hidden behind it.

**Line of action per strike frame:**
- **Frame 1:** he leans back to the upper-left onto the rear (screen-left) leg. The hand rises beside the head and the tip points up and back, at (44,23).
- **Frame 2 (hold):** he coils back and crouches. The sword is cocked behind the head with the blade pointing back to the screen-left, tip at (29,57); the hand is hidden behind the head and the elbow shows. The shield is tucked in.
- **Frame 3 (smear):** the front foot steps from (98,123) to (107,124) and the torso whips forward while the head lags. The arm crosses the chest and the blade is level, pointing right, tip at (132,76).
- **Frame 4 (contact):** he lunges low with the rear leg straight and the arm fully out. The blade runs from (101,90) to (132,107), nearly parallel to the (96,48) ground line toward the target tile and well clear of the body. The shield arm has swung back behind the head.
- **Frame 5:** the tip finishes at (127,120) near the ground. The shield lags a frame behind the sword.

The tip slows into the follow-through: it moves 31 px, then 14 px.

**Death fall.** He staggers to the upper-left, kneels with the sword tip grounded at the lower-right, then falls back. The corpse lies head upper-left, feet lower-right; the sword lies at the lower-right and the shield lies flat on the far side.

**Compromises:**
- The head-to-feet line is about 30°, not 26.6°, because the head is lifted off the ground rather than sunk into it.
- The far foot of the corpse is at y 118, because the ground there is farther back and so higher on screen.
- The flinch-1 blade is shortened by 15% to suggest it pointing away from the viewer.

I made the near pose set for the swordsman, who faces lower-right. Every strike, flinch and death now moves the way he is looking. All the checks pass:
- **Frames:** counts are 4/8/4/8. Idle frame 0 and strike frame 0 are exactly REST, and death frame 0 equals flinch frame 0.
- **Small-motion frames:** strike 7 and flinch 3 stay within 1.4 px of REST.
- **Per frame:** every frame has `facing: lower-right`, `far: l` and its own `order`.
- **Files:** only `cand_3` was written.

**Line of action per strike frame:**
- **1:** leans back toward the upper-left. The fist is beside the back of the head with the tip pointing up and back.
- **2 (wind-up):** crouched and coiled. The fist is behind the head, the blade hangs down-left behind the shoulders, and the shield is tucked across the belly.
- **3 (smear):** the torso whips round as the front (far) foot lands. The fist passes the chin and the blade points level to the right.
- **4 (contact):** one diagonal from the shield, swung back behind the shoulders at the upper-left, through the extended near arm to the blade tip at the lower-right. The blade is at 30°, close to the 26.6° attack line. The front knee is bent and the rear leg straight.
- **5:** the blade carries on down until the tip is just above the ground at the lower-right.
- **6:** he rises and the sword comes back up on the near side.

**The tip's path:** down-left behind him, over the top, level to the right, then down to the lower-right. The blade never crosses the head or torso at contact.

**Death:** he staggers back toward the upper-left with the sword flung up, then kneels with the tip resting on the ground at the lower-right. He falls back reaching behind him with the near hand. The corpse lies on its back at about 26°, head upper-left and feet lower-right, legs spread in a V. The shield lies flat at the upper-right and the sword on the ground at the lower-right.

**Compromises:**
- The arm is stretched about 30% in strike 1–3 so the fist clears the head.
- In strike 3 the near arm crosses the chin.
- In death 2–3 the blade crosses in front of the knees.
- The shield in strike 4–5 sits behind the back and may read as slung there.
- The rear leg in strike 4–5 is foreshortened.

verdicts.summary: All three candidates obey the rule. At strike contact the blade points about 27-30 degrees below horizontal to the lower-right, which is close to the iso angle. Every flinch snaps the head and torso toward the upper-left, every corpse lies with its head at the upper-left and feet at the lower-right, and every dropped sword is at the lower-right. Idle 0 and strike 0 match the sprite's pose exactly in all three, and the idle data is identical across them. Idle 1-3, strike 7 and flinch 3 all stay within 2 px of rest. C is best in all three rows. Its shield swings back behind the torso, which is the correct counter-swing for this facing and leaves the blade path clear. The sword arm reads clearly at f3, the wind-up blade really hangs down behind the shoulders, the flinch knees bend in the right direction, and the death has the strongest stagger and slump with clean blade/shield separation. B has the most powerful body mechanics (deepest coil and lunge, consistent limb lengths) and the cleanest corpse line. Its flaws are a hidden arm at strike f3, a level wind-up blade, bow-legged knees in several frames, a layering bug at death d1 (far arm over the shield) and a blade crossing the shield at d2-d3. A is the weakest: stiff legs and little crouch, a sword arm stretched up to 60%, a blade crossing the shield at strike f3-f5 and death d2-d3, a sword shrunk 30% in flinch f0-f1, a backward-bent leg at death d4, and corpse legs heaped together. Fixer suggestions for C: borrow B's deeper f4-f5 lunge, add an in-between for the shield's return at f6, show a sliver of the far forearm at f3, and at d3 put both knees and the sword tip on the ground. One shared flaw in all three: the sword is already lying in its final spot at death d4, so the 'slips out of the hand' beat is missing.

verdicts.summary:
All three candidates obey the rule. Each one strikes toward the lower-right (contact tip at about (132,105) every time), takes the hit from the lower-right with the head snapping to the upper-left, and dies falling to the upper-left. The corpse lies near the 2:1 iso axis (head-to-feet slope 0.45-0.58) with the sword dropped at the lower-right. idle 0 and strike 0 match the sprite exactly in all three. idle 1-3, strike 7 and flinch 3 stay within about 2 px (body joints at most 1.4 px off), so every candidate passes the settle check.

B is the best set overall. It follows the beats most closely: an overhead lift in f1, a true cocked wind-up with the blade hanging down behind in f2, a level smear in f3 with the arm clearly extended, and an X silhouette at contact. Its layering is the cleanest, with no blade-over-shield or hand-over-head merges. It also has the best stagger, buckle and kneel in death, and its flinch knees bend forward correctly.

B's main fixes:
- Shorten the stretched sword arm in strike f1-f3 (13.0/11.7 px against 9.5/7.8 at rest).
- Make the shield swinging behind to screen-left in strike f3-f5 readable, or tone it down.
- Rest the sword tip on the ground in death d3.
- Flatten the splayed far leg in d5-d7.

A has the most powerful contact: the deepest lunge, with arm lengths true to rest. Its weaknesses:
- Its f3 arm disappears into the collar and shield.
- Its f4-f5 shield merges with the face.
- Its knees bow backward in strike f1-f3, flinch f1 and death d1.
- Its f2 blade is level, not hanging down.
- Its d3 kneel is cluttered, and the dropped sword touches the feet.

A's lunge legs from f4-f5 would be a good transplant into B. C is the weakest:
- Its arm is stretched by up to 60%.
- In strike f2 the hand sits on top of the head.
- The strike is upright and has little power.
- The blade crosses the shield face in strike f4-f5 and death d2-d3.
- The flinch sword is shortened to dagger length.
- The death legs are bunched up.

verdicts.summary:
All three candidates follow the rule. Each strike lands toward the lower-right at -27 to -30 degrees, close to the isometric lower-right of -26.6. The flinch snaps the head toward the upper-left, and the body falls with the head upper-left and the feet and sword lower-right. In every candidate, idle 0 and strike 0 match the rest pose exactly, flinch 0 equals death 0, and the warp frames (idle 1-3, strike 7, flinch 3) stay within 2.24 px of rest.

Strike, best C (8): it is the only candidate that keeps the sword-arm length constant (about 17-18 px). Its deep lunge contact reads as the most powerful, and its shield stays clear of the sword. It loses points for the level wind-up blade in frame 2 and the near knee bending backward in frames 1-3.
- A (7.5) follows the beats most literally (the wind-up blade hangs behind the shoulders, there is a real coil, and the foot steps 12 px). But its arm stretches by up to 43%, its shield jumps to screen-left in frames 3-5 and pops back in frame 6, and frame 5 nearly repeats frame 4.
- B (5.5) has a weak coil and an upright contact pose, its arm stretches by about 45%, and its sword hand sits on the shield in frames 3-5.

Flinch, best A (8): it keeps the sword at full length, both arms are flung out strongly, and the knees bend forward correctly in frame 1. C (7) has backward-bending knees in frame 1. B (5.5) shrinks the blade to a dagger and pulls the shield back in.

Death, best A (8): it has the strongest stagger, the cleanest layering in frames 2-3 (the blade stays off the shield) and a corpse that lies along the isometric axis. Its fixes are a tip that hovers in frame 3 and a sword that slopes off the axis in frames 5-7. C (7) puts the tip on the ground and lays the sword on the axis, but the blade crosses the shield in frames 2-3 and the hilt touches the boot in frames 4-7. B (5) has knees that don't fold, a merged shield and sword, a jumble of legs, and a sword left hanging in mid-air.

The final near set is built and rendered: all four animations come from cand_3, with most of the judges' flaws fixed. Idle 0 and strike 0 are exactly REST. Idle 1-3 are identical to the far set's breathing frames. Death 0 equals flinch 0. The settle frames stay within 1.4 px of REST.

**Taken:** idle is cand_3's, which is identical to the far set and the other two candidates. Strike, flinch and death are cand_3's, then fixed.

**Strike, fixed:**
- **f1-f2 weight:** the pelvis now sits at x77, then x75, over the rear leg, and the f2 crouch is deeper.
- **f1-f3 arm stretch:** the sword arm is back to about 9.5/9 px (rest is 9.5/7.8).

- **f3 hand:** stays at shoulder level.

- **f5 follow-through:** no longer a copy of f4. The hand travels 11 px and the blade turns to 45° with the tip at the ground. It stops at 45° rather than the suggested 55° because 55° would cut across the front knee.
- **f3-f5 shield:** the far forearm is now drawn over the shield (showing its inside), so it reads as held by the far arm. It is also moved clear of the near shoulder.
- **f6:** a new in-between with the shield tucked across the belly.

**Strike, left:**
- The shield still goes behind him to screen-left. One judge praised this as the correct counter-swing, and putting it at the back-right collides with the forward-leaning head and the blade.
- The 25 px shield jump from f2 to f3 stays, because f3 is the 50 ms smear frame.

**Flinch, fixed:** at f0 the chest goes back 5 px, the shield is flung 4 px further out relative to the body, and the blade tip is 9 px higher. At f1 the lean is deeper and the pelvis drops 6 px. The shield is drawn in front of the torso, as in idle.

**Flinch, left:** f3 keeps head_tilt 2. That gives a gentle 5, 2, 0 settle, the same as the far set.

**Death, fixed:**
- **d2:** the near shin and both forearms are back to normal length, with 3.8 px between the blade and the shield.
- **d3:** both knees and the sword tip are on the ground.
- **d4:** the sword is in the air, mid-fall.
- **d5-d7:** the far leg lies along the ground axis. The dropped sword now lies on the 2:1 ground axis, parallel to the body and apart from the feet, rather than crosswise as one judge suggested; parallel gives a smooth d4 to d5 drop.

**Death, left:** the shorter head/neck at d2-d3 and the shorter shins at d1 are left, since they read as a slumped or angled-away pose.
